--the son of बृहस्पति; deputed by gods to learn सम्जीविनी विद्या from शुक्राचार्य; offered himself as a disciple and admitted as a pupil by शुक्र; conducted himself to the satisfaction of his teacher and his daughter देवयानी for a period of ५०० years. Once while out in the woods tending शुक्र's cows, the Asuras killed him and left his body to be devoured by dogs and jackals. The cows returned home but not Kaca. देवयानी suspected of foul play and reported his death. शुक्र brought him back to life.
1: M. २५. १४-37.
On another occasion he went to the woods to gather flowers for देवयानी and this time the Asuras ground him to pieces and mixing them with सुरा offered it to शुक्र who drank it. Again देवयानी persisted wanting him back to life. This meant शुक्र's death for he had to come out by tearing open his belly. So he taught Kaca the सम्जीविनी विद्या so that he might restore him after his revival. Thus he did and so he learnt the विद्या। After a sojourn of ten hundred years he returned with due leave from his teacher. Now देवयानी offered to marry him but he pointed out that it was not proper to marry his preceptor's daughter. So [page१-299+ २५] she cursed that he would not get the fruits of his विद्या and he retorted that she would not find a ब्राह्मण husband but only a क्षत्रिय. Returned to the gods who gave him a share in their oblations; put to death by वृषपर्वन्'s men.
2: M. २५. ३८-69; chap. २६ whole; भा. IX. १८. २२.
--the नाग presiding over the month of माधव। भा. XII. ११. ३४.
(I)--a son of विश्वामित्र. Br. III. ६६. ६९; वा. ९१. ९७; Vi.
(III)--one of the eight निधिस् of Kubera. वा. ४१. १०.
--the सर्प who resides in the sun's chariot during the month of माधव। Vi. II. १०. 5.
--a Janapada of the केतुमाल Continent. वा. ४४. १५.
